thread:
maria: quick q — ran into a weird one: a customer API key that contains a ':' is causing our Basic auth checks to fail in the Go client. header we send vs what the service expects don't match. anyone seen colon/newline gotchas?

ryan: yup. lots of places this trips folks. two big buckets: (1) how you form the user:pass string before base64 and (2) accidental newlines/CRLF introduced by echo/build args/k8s secrets. both will make the base64 different.

jess: fwiw we avoid Basic when keys are freeform. prefer Authorization: Bearer <KEY>. but if you must do Basic (legacy service) the canonical thing is to pick a stable username (eg "api") and put the key as the password: "api:${KEY}" then base64 that.

maria: ah ok. customer can't change their service so we have to send Basic. our code does something like:  ```go req.SetBasicAuth("", apiKey) ``` and curl tests looked fine locally but failed in CI.

ryan: SetBasicAuth("", apiKey) is fine if you actually produce the same bytes. two common CI/docker/k8s gotchas: 
- echo adds a newline unless you use -n or printf. so if you do `API_KEY=$(cat /tmp/keyfile)` and that file has a trailing newline, the string used in build may include it.
- Docker build args sometimes get CRLF from Windows hosts; you end up with \r at the end.

jess: example fixes: 
```
# safe shell read (no newline)
API_KEY=$(printf '%s' "$(cat secret.txt)")
# or when encoding explicitly
AUTH=$(printf '%s' "api:${API_KEY}" | base64)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic ${AUTH}" https://... 
```
also if you're creating k8s secret: `kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-literal=key="$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY")"` (avoid files with trailing newline).

maria: that explains curl vs CI mismatch — CI secret was stored as a file with a newline. we used `cat` directly in the Dockerfile ARG and forgot `-n`. will patch. anything else that bites?

ryan: Windows CRLF is sneaky. In a GitHub Actions workflow, secrets passed into `::set-env` or into files can pick up \r. Quick normalize: `tr -d '\r'` when you write the secret into a file during the build.

jess: also watch language libraries: some helpers will URL-encode credentials when assembling auth headers for HTTP URIs (not Basic header). Eg if you pass credentials into a library that then constructs a `https://user:pass@host` url, the colon in the password may get percent-encoded in the URL and then the header built from that will differ. So avoid building auth via URL embedding.

maria: oof. our .NET integration uses `new NetworkCredential(user, pass)` then `CredentialCache` — does that handle colons/newlines fine?

ryan: NetworkCredential will use the raw strings when building Basic header (it just combines user:pass then base64), so colons in the password are fine there. The main problem is when something in the pipeline mutates the string (newlines, CRLF, url-encoding, trimming).

maria: thanks. I'll do these fixes: normalize on read, use `printf`/`echo -n`, strip CR, and switch tests to use `printf` when creating k8s secrets in CI.

deploy-bot: rotation scheduled for customer-12345 keys at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z — reminder: if you change how clients encode headers, coordinate with support. (reacted with :bell:)

jess: one more nit — if you can't change the service and the key contains a colon at the *start* (eg ":abc"), then explicitly set a username (can't rely on empty username). `api:${KEY}` is safest.

maria: perfect. will push patch and add a small note to the SDK README about newlines/CRLF and the preferred `Authorization: Bearer` fallback. thanks all :thumbsup:
